claim:
PR title: fix(runner): retry the WAL pragma when another opener holds the lock

## Problem

Two processes opening one fresh `state/` directory still lose a race, with
`database is locked`. `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL` is the one statement left
outside #164's `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, and unlike an ordinary statement it does not
wait out `busy_timeout`: when the first opener holds the lock it fails at once.
So `runner-flows (2/2)` could still flake `main` for the same class of reason
that stopped the merge queue earlier (the `duplicate column name` flake).

Measured on `main` at `495c1cd1`, two concurrent `State` openers on a fresh
directory: 7 of 100 rounds failed with `database is locked`; every failure was
at the `journal_mode` pragma, none at `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`.

## Fix

The pragma now retries on SQLite's busy error (`errcode` 5) alone, every 5 ms,
for up to the same 5 s as `busy_timeout`, then rethrows. Any other error is
raised immediately. #164's single-transaction migration path is unchanged: the
`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` / `migrate()` / `COMMIT` block follows the pragma as before.
The lean-core baseline is untouched; the change fits under it.

With the retry: 0 of 300 rounds failed.

## Test

`services/runner/test/state-concurrent-open.test.mjs` starts a process that
holds the write lock on a fresh state directory's file while it is still in
rollback mode, then opens the same directory through `State` from a second
process and asserts both exit cleanly. It fails on `main` with
`database is locked` and passes with this change.
